title: The installer asks which paths to govern, whether to run pip and whether to commit, and has a no-questions mode

context.task: Second contract of the one-command installer (ROADMAP V2, ADR-008). tools/install.py already copies the kit, merges the settings (permissions, hooks, includeGitInstructions, a strict sandbox with a denyWrite per governed path), installs the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks and reports whether the validator's interpreter has the pinned pydantic, printing the pip command without running it. It gains the three questions ADR-008 allows (which paths to govern besides the minimum, permission to run that pip command, whether to commit what it installed), flags that answer them in advance, and a no-questions mode for the CI and the tests. INSTALL.md is rewritten by the executing agent afterwards, not here.

select.heading: ADR-008 — La instalación en una orden, con el entorno fuera del repositorio (2026-10-12, autor)

problem: ADR-008 decided an installation in one command that asks only which paths to govern besides the minimum and whether to commit, asks before it runs pip, and has a mode without questions. Today tools/install.py asks nothing: it always governs the minimum (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/**, .mcp.json, tools/**), a person who wants more must edit .actuarii.json and the denyWrite list by hand and keep them in step, it prints the pip command and leaves it to the person, and it ends with 'commit the installed files' as a step the person must do. An existing .actuarii.json that is not exactly the example is a conflict, so a second run over a repository that governs more paths would stop.
decisions: D1 Flags. The command line gains --govern PATH (repeatable, in the order given), --install-pydantic, --commit and --no-input; --dry-run and the target stay as they are.

D2 When the installer asks. It asks only in a real run without --no-input. A flag answers its question in advance: with any --govern the paths question is not asked, with --install-pydantic the pip question is answered yes, with --commit the commit question is answered yes. A dry run and --no-input ask nothing, and what no flag says is no (no other path, no pip, no commit). Each answer is one line read from stdin; the end of input answers the default (no other path, no, no). A question is written on stderr only when stdin is a terminal; the answers are read the same way when it is not, so that a script or a test can pipe them. A run that asks nothing, and a run whose stdin is empty, write exactly what they write today on stdout and on stderr.

D3 The paths question, asked before the plan is built (so before any write and before conflicts are looked for). It names what is already governed (the minimum, then the extra paths of an existing configuration, D5) and asks for other paths, one per line, each a file path or a directory followed by /**, an empty line or the end of input to finish. An answer is stripped of surrounding whitespace; an answer that D4 refuses is not taken, a line on stderr (whether or not stdin is a terminal) starting with the installer's prefix gives the answer and why, and reading goes on.

D4 Accepted entries, for --govern and for answers alike. An entry is either a plain path or a plain path followed by /**, where the plain path is not empty, does not start with / or ~, holds no '..', no backslash, no control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F) and none of * ? [ ] { }, does not end with /, has no empty or '.' segment, and does not start with the segment .git or .data (the git directory and the audit trail are not governed paths). A plain path without /** that names an existing directory of the target is refused, with the advice to write it followed by /**. An entry that is already governed (in the minimum or among the existing extras) or given twice counts once. A --govern argument that is refused is a problem: exit 2, the argument and the reason on stderr, nothing written and nothing asked.

D5 The configuration. The extras are the extra paths of an existing configuration (below), then the accepted entries of this run that are not already there, in order. The installer writes EXAMPLE_CONFIG with governed_paths = the minimum in its order followed by the extras. An existing .actuarii.json is adopted when it equals EXAMPLE_CONFIG in every key but governed_paths, and its governed_paths are the minimum in its order followed by entries that D4 accepts, ignoring the directory check, without duplicates: those entries are its extra paths. Adopted with no new entry, it is skipped as today; adopted with new entries, it is written with them appended (a merge, reported under write:). Any other existing .actuarii.json is a conflict, with today's message.

D6 denyWrite. The entries the installer merges into sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite are today's plus, for each extra path, "./" followed by the path without a trailing /** (the rule of tests/security/test_sandbox_settings.py deny_entry), each once, sorted as today. A second run with the same extras writes nothing.

D7 pip. In a real run, after the writes, when the check ran and printed a pydantic other than the pin (another version or none), and neither the executable it printed nor the prefix it printed lies inside the target (resolved physically): the question "install pydantic==<pin> into <executable> with <command>? [y/N]", or --install-pydantic. y or yes, in any case, is yes; anything else is no. On yes the installer runs [executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "pydantic==<pin>"] through tools.audit.run_process, from the target, with its own environment and a timeout of 600 s. The report then has a line "pip: <command> exited <status>", or "pip: <command> did not finish within 600 seconds", or "pip: <command> could not be run: <error>", followed, when it exited 0, by the python lines of a new check; when it did not exit 0, the line also gives the last non-empty line of its stderr, and the installer exits 1 after the report. When the executable or the prefix lies inside the target, nothing is asked or run: the python lines already say the environment belongs outside. A dry run never runs pip; with --install-pydantic and a check that is not the pin, its report says "pip: a real run would run <command>". The pip command is the one the python line prints today.

D8 The commit. In a real run that wrote at least one file of the working tree (any write but the git hooks), last, the question "commit the installed files now, as \"Install Actuarii\"? [y/N]", or --commit; same answers as D7. On yes the installer runs git add -- <those paths> and then git commit -q -m "Install Actuarii" -- <those paths> in the target, where <those paths> are the labels of this run's writes in the working tree, so that nothing else staged or untracked goes into the commit. The pre-commit and commit-msg hooks it installed run on that commit. Success: a report line "commit: <abbreviated hash of HEAD> Install Actuarii". Failure of either git command: "commit: failed: <the git command> exited <status>: <its stderr on one line>", and the installer exits 1 after the report.

D9 The report. After the python lines and before the closing: the pip lines (D7), then the commit line (D8). The next steps of a real run lose the step "commit the installed files" when the commit succeeded, and are renumbered from 1; otherwise they stay word for word. A run with no question asked and no flag of D1 prints exactly what it prints today.

D10 Exit statuses: 0 when all went well; 1 for conflicts (nothing written, nothing asked after the paths question), a write that fails, pip that fails and a commit that fails; 2 for the problems of today and a refused --govern. The module docstring and the argparse help describe the flags, the questions and the no-questions mode.

D11 Tests. Every test drives the installer as a process (tests/unit/test_installer.py install()), with the answers piped on stdin where it asks, a fake interpreter as today's Fake where pip is involved (one that records each call and answers the second check with the pin after pip ran), and a git identity in the environment or the HOME's .gitconfig where the installer commits. A test where the installer commits runs it with a PATH whose python3 is the interpreter of the test run and that does not hold the session's Python shim, as test_the_installed_kit_is_committed_with_its_own_hook_and_head_holds_the_shim_names_as_equal_executables does: the hooks the installer installed run on that commit, and the shim of this repository refuses the target's scripts. The tests of today keep passing unchanged: a run without flags and with empty stdin behaves as today. No text in tools/ or tests/ cites a clause of AGENTS.md (tests/unit/test_kit_independence.py).
D12 Not in this contract: INSTALL.md, the session announcement, the commit-msg hook and the gate (done by the acta-en-git contract), the user's own settings.

D13 The validator requires a Rationale in every proposal: include it, even if the schema of validate_proposal shown to you lacks it. Your governed writes are recorded in the audit trail, and once the person installed the commit-msg hook, your commit carries its record: that is expected.
D14 No new dependency and no file outside files_may_touch.

D15 Gates: red-first, each red test seen failing for its stated reason before the change that makes it pass; full-suite, `pytest tests/` exits 0 at the commit; verify-red-green, tools/audit/verify_red_green.py exits 0 on the report.

behaviours.statement: --govern and the answers to the paths question add accepted entries to governed_paths after the minimum and their denyWrite entries; a refused --govern exits 2 and writes nothing; a refused answer is explained and asked again.

A configuration the installer wrote with extra paths is adopted by the next run, which writes nothing when nothing new is asked and appends what is new otherwise; any other configuration is still a conflict.

pip runs only after a yes or --install-pydantic, only in a real run, only for an interpreter whose executable and prefix lie outside the target, with the exact command the report prints; its result and a new check are reported, and its failure exits 1.

The commit happens only after a yes or --commit, holds exactly the working-tree files this run wrote, runs the installed hooks, is reported, and removes the commit step from the next steps; its failure exits 1.
--no-input and a dry run ask nothing; a run with empty stdin and no flag behaves exactly as today.

tests.must_catch: a --govern entry missing from governed_paths or from denyWrite, out of order or twice; an already governed entry added again; a refused --govern (each rule of D4, the directory without /** included) that does not exit 2 with its reason or that writes anything
tests.reason: at base the installer has no --govern option: argparse exits 2 with unrecognized arguments in place of the reason, and nothing is governed beyond the minimum

tests.must_catch: answers to the paths question not taken as --govern entries are; a refused answer not explained on stderr or that stops the questions; the end of input not ending them; the question written on stderr when stdin is not a terminal
tests.reason: at base the installer reads nothing from stdin

tests.must_catch: a second run over a configuration with extra paths that conflicts or writes; a run with a new entry that does not append it to the adopted configuration and its denyWrite; a configuration that differs in another key, or whose extras D4 refuses, that is not a conflict
tests.reason: at base any configuration other than the example is a conflict

tests.must_catch: pip run without a yes or --install-pydantic, in a dry run, for an executable or prefix inside the target, or with another command or directory; a yes that does not run it; a missing pip line or new check; a failure that does not exit 1; a question when the check says it has the pin
tests.reason: at base the installer never runs pip and has no --install-pydantic

tests.must_catch: a commit made without a yes or --commit; a commit that holds other staged or untracked files, misses one written file or has another message; next steps that keep the commit step after a commit or lose it without one; a commit failure that does not exit 1 or is not reported
tests.reason: at base the installer never commits and has no --commit

tests.must_catch: a question asked, or stdin read, under --no-input or in a dry run; flags that do not answer their questions in advance
tests.reason: at base there is no --no-input and none of the flags

tests.must_catch: a change to what holds today: the files a default run writes, the conflicts, the dry run and its parity with the real run, the next steps, the python lines, the warnings, the system Python
tests.reason: they hold at base and must keep holding: every test of tests/unit/test_installer.py as it is at base, and tests/security/test_sandbox_settings.py

commit_message: feat(instalador): pregunta qué gobernar, pip y el commit, con un modo sin preguntas
